name: @projexlight/sdk-deliverability
summary: Suppression, opt-out & DNC plane for every outbound channel (P14·E3). Holds a reason-tagged do-not-contact list that send paths query before delivering, issues single-purpose unsubscribe tokens, ingests provider bounce/complaint webhooks (SES, SendGrid, Mailgun, Postmark, Twilio) that auto-suppress hard bounces and complaints, syncs inbound IMAP replies with pause-on-reply, and tracks per-(tenant,channel) sender reputation that auto-pauses a channel when the bounce or complaint rate crosses threshold. PII-safe: recipients are matched by sha256 address_hash and/or the L4 subject_persona_id, and opt-out tokens persist only a token_hash — never a raw email, phone, or plaintext token.

endpoints.description: Pre-send enforcement: return whether a single {address} or a batch of {addresses[]} is suppressed for the tenant (or globally) on a channel; call before every send.
Add (or refresh) a reason-tagged suppression for an address on a channel, at tenant or global scope, with optional expiry.
List a tenant's suppressions plus global rows, optionally filtered by channel and limited.
Remove (un-suppress) an address for a channel at the given scope so it becomes contactable again.
Mint a single-purpose opt-out (unsubscribe/resubscribe/preferences) token; the raw token is returned exactly once and only its hash is stored.
Redeem an opt-out token one time: suppress the address and write an opt-out event; 410 Gone if the token is unknown, already used, or expired.
Register or rotate a tenant's HMAC signing secret for a provider's inbound bounce/complaint webhook.
Public provider bounce/complaint webhook receiver (HMAC-verified when a secret is configured); tenant carried via ?tenant_id=, hard bounces and complaints auto-suppress the recipient.
List a tenant's processed bounce/complaint events, optionally filtered by classification and limited.
Register a per-tenant IMAP mailbox config that the reply worker polls for inbound replies.
List a tenant's configured IMAP mailboxes.
Poll a mailbox once over IMAP via the pluggable fetcher (no-op without a live client); 404 when the mailbox is unknown.
Ingest a single inbound reply (what the IMAP worker calls per message): classify, record, and fire pause-on-reply for human replies.
List a tenant's captured inbound reply events, optionally filtered by classification and limited.
Record send outcomes (sent/delivered/bounced/complained) for a channel and recompute reputation status, auto-pausing when the bounce/complaint rate crosses threshold.
Return reputation signals for a tenant across all channels, or a single channel via ?channel=.
Manually resume a paused channel (human override), clearing the pause and resetting the window; 404 when no reputation row exists.

models.description: Reason-tagged do-not-contact list keyed by address_hash (+ optional subject_persona_id) per channel; scope='tenant' rows carry a tenant_id, scope='global' rows are tenant-less and suppress across all tenants.
Single-purpose unsubscribe/resubscribe/preferences token; only the sha256 token_hash is stored and used_at makes it one-time.
Append-only audit of every opt-out / complaint action, linking the redeemed token and resulting suppression.
Per-(tenant,provider) HMAC signing key + algo used to verify inbound bounce/complaint webhooks; UNIQUE(tenant_id, provider).
Append-only audit of processed provider notifications classified as hard_bounce/soft_bounce/complaint/delivered/other; hard bounces and complaints auto-suppress.
Per-tenant IMAP mailbox config the reply worker polls incrementally via uid_validity + last_uid; UNIQUE(tenant_id, username, folder).
Captured inbound reply thread-matched via In-Reply-To/References; human replies set paused_sequence. UNIQUE(mailbox_id, message_id) makes re-polling idempotent.
One row per (tenant, channel) with running send/delivery/bounce/complaint counters, derived rates, and a good|watch|paused status that auto-pauses over threshold.

scenarios.title: Check suppression before every send
scenarios.when_to_use: In the send path, immediately before delivering an email or SMS, to skip any recipient who is suppressed for the tenant or globally.
scenarios.expected_outcome: Returns 200 with data.results as an array of { address, suppressed } for the batch; sendable holds only the addresses that are not on the suppression list.

scenarios.title: Add a suppression from the service layer
scenarios.when_to_use: When another SDK or worker needs to add a do-not-contact entry in-process (e.g. after a manual DNC request) without going through HTTP.
scenarios.expected_outcome: A deliverability.suppression row is upserted (address stored only as address_hash) and the subsequent isSuppressed check returns true for that tenant/channel/address.

scenarios.title: Redeem an unsubscribe token from an email link
scenarios.when_to_use: When a recipient clicks the one-click unsubscribe link and the public opt-out page posts the token back to suppress them.
scenarios.expected_outcome: A valid token returns 200 { data: { redeemed: true } } and suppresses the address plus writes an optout_event; a spent or expired token returns 410 Gone so the page can render an already-unsubscribed state.

scenarios.title: Auto-suppress on a provider bounce webhook
scenarios.when_to_use: When an email/SMS provider (SES, SendGrid, Mailgun, Postmark, Twilio) posts a bounce/complaint notification to the tenant's per-provider webhook URL.
scenarios.expected_outcome: The signature is verified when a secret is configured (401 on mismatch), a bounce_event audit row is written, and hard bounces/complaints auto-suppress the recipient so no future send reaches them.

compliance_posture.notes: Enforces opt-out / do-not-contact obligations for outbound email and SMS (CAN-SPAM one-click unsubscribe, honoured suppressions). PII-safe by design: recipients are matched by sha256 address_hash and/or the L4 subject_persona_id and are never stored as raw email/phone; opt-out tokens persist only a token_hash. Suppressions and opt-out/bounce audits are append-friendly and tenant-scoped (with an explicit cross-tenant global scope). Webhook signing secrets are stored inline in the SDK today and should point at the sdk-secrets vault in production.
